subject: Zenlyx discovery recap & procurement outline
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@zenlyx.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Zenlyx discovery recap & procurement outline

Alex — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap so we have alignment and a clear path into procurement. Notes below are intentionally concise; I can expand any section you’d like.

Key pain points you shared:
- Latency variability on your customer-facing chat experience during peak hours (10–20% of sessions exceed SLA).
- High per-token costs from current setup (mix of hosted API + burst to on-prem) that make scaling expensive.
- Lack of consistent rollout tools for model updates across prod/staging leading to regressions.

Current stack (what you confirmed):
- Frontend chat app (React) -> backend orchestrator -> OpenAI-hosted endpoints + fallback to a private GPU pool for high-volume flows.
- Redis for session state + a homegrown prefix cache.
- CI/CD for models is manual; no structured canaries for inference.

Primary success criteria (what Zenlyx would call a win):
1) 99th percentile inference latency < 250ms for core flows at 95% of expected traffic.
2) 30–40% reduction in per-conversation inference spend through caching, batching, and smarter routing.
3) Safe model rollouts with ability to A/B and automatic fallback.

Immediate next steps (procurement-focused):
- Please confirm the procurement/eval stakeholders and timeline (who signs, who evaluates compliance). You mentioned Daniel Wu (procurement) and Priya Shah (security) — please confirm.
- I'll send a short procurement framing doc that includes: decision process steps, typical docs we provide (SOC2 summary, data handling), and an initial commercial guardrail (capacity/reserved pool vs on-demand cost ranges).
- If the timeline is Q2 commitment, let us know any internal budget windows or required PO terms.

Initial commercial guardrails (rough, non-binding):
- Typical entry: reserved capacity commitment for sustained workloads (monthly committed GPUs) with burst-to-hosted for peaks.
- Band: ballpark $40k–$120k ARR equivalent for the first 6–12 months depending on capacity and SLA tier; we can refit after an initial quarter based on usage.

Attachments: discovery-notes-zenlyx.pdf (one-page summary).

Would you please: 1) confirm procurement contact(s) and timing, and 2) share any mandatory compliance docs we should prep before the procurement meeting?

Thanks — happy to hop on a short follow-up with Daniel and Priya if that helps move things faster.

—
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0132

Subject: Re: Zenlyx discovery recap & procurement outline

Thanks Jordan — this is super helpful and captures the conversation. Confirming a few items:

- Stakeholders: Daniel Wu (procurement) will run the contracting process; Priya Shah will triage security and compliance questions. I'll coordinate technical evals (I own the PoC).
- Timeline: target decision by the end of Q2 (we have a budget cutoff mid-June). Aim for an initial reserved capacity pilot starting early July if we sign.
- Success criteria: align with your bullets — latency improvements and 30%+ cost reduction are must-haves. Also need clear rollback/canary behavior for model changes.

Priya — for compliance, we need SOC2 Type II evidence plus clarity on data residency for customer logs. Daniel — once Jordan shares the procurement framing, I’ll route to you for initial commercial feasibility.

Two quick asks for Jordan: can you provide a one-page procurement/contract checklist and a high-level SKU table (committed pool vs on-demand) so procurement has an early read on order-of-magnitude costs? We don't need a full quote yet, just a guardrail.

On the technical side, happy to run a PoC with a 2-week traffic window. I'll need a short runbook for the integration and the default model variants we should test.

—Alex
Alex Morgan
Head of Platform Integrations, Zenlyx
alex.morgan@zenlyx.io
